narratives.name: Team Alpha Narrative
narratives.description: Team Topologies context for baseline Team alpha

narrativeContexts.context: Team Topologies treats the team as the fundamental unit of delivery, not individuals, with team-first thinking applied to all design decisions including software boundaries and cognitive load limits.

Four team types provide simplified vocabulary: stream-aligned teams own value streams end-to-end, platform teams reduce cognitive load via self-service, enabling teams temporarily boost capabilities, complicated-subsystem teams handle specialist complexity. Teams interact through three explicit modes (Collaboration, X-as-a-Service, Facilitating) with Team APIs defining interfaces. Cognitive load management ensures teams sized and scoped within human bandwidth limits (5-9 people, maximum 1 complex or 2-3 simple domains). Teams function as organizational sensors with performance metrics signaling when topology evolution needed.

Effective teams require stability (weeks-to-months), clear ownership boundaries, explicit interaction modes, and continuous cognitive load optimization to deliver fast flow and serve as foundation for intentional architecture through Conway's Law.

narratives.name: Way Of Working Narrative
narratives.description: Team Topologies context for baseline Way Of Working alpha

narrativeContexts.context: Team Topologies defines only three ways teams should interact, eliminating ambiguous coordination mandates and providing clear vocabulary for team relationships.

Collaboration mode suits discovery with high bandwidth but high cognitive cost, time-bounded with clear goals. X-as-a-Service provides predictable low-interaction consumption with DevEx focus, requiring well-defined boundaries. Facilitating empowers teams toward self-sufficiency through coaching, not execution. Modes evolve over time as teams mature and systems stabilize, with interaction effectiveness measured to optimize cognitive load. Team APIs formalize interaction surfaces including code interfaces, versioning, practices, and communication norms. Supporting practices include continuous delivery, test-first development, and You Built It You Run It ownership.

Explicit interaction modes with strategic evolution enable fast flow by minimizing wasteful coordination while preserving necessary collaboration, with organizational sensing driving continuous improvement.

narratives.name: Practice Overview Narrative
narratives.description: High-level practice context using Hero's Journey framework

narrativeContexts.context: Organizations struggle with static hierarchical teams causing bottlenecks, dependencies, and misalignment between communication structures and system architecture.
Recognition that team structure determines software architecture and value flow speed, requiring intentional organizational design using four fundamental team types.
Teams optimize cognitive load through domain boundaries and platform abstraction, with explicit interaction modes (Collaboration, X-as-a-Service, Facilitating) defining how teams work together.
Team APIs formalize interaction surfaces, enabling teams to function as sensors providing performance signals that drive continuous topology evolution through small incremental changes.
Sustained team effectiveness with demonstrable productivity gains through cognitive load optimization, clear ownership boundaries, and architecture aligned with team structure.

narratives.name: Cognitive Load Narrative
narratives.description: Cognitive load management in Team Topologies

narrativeContexts.context: Teams have finite cognitive capacity that gets exhausted when responsibilities exceed working memory limits, with three types of load (intrinsic task complexity, extraneous environment overhead, germane productive learning) requiring active management.

Cognitive load management applies domain heuristics (maximum 1 complex or 2-3 simple domains per team), platform abstraction as primary reduction mechanism for extraneous load (infrastructure concerns), consistent UX across services to minimize learning overhead, and regular assessments asking 'Do you feel effective and able to respond timely?' Overloaded teams make poor decisions and move slowly despite competence, with symptoms including context switching, inability to maintain mastery, and ineffectiveness despite skill. Platform teams measure success primarily through cognitive load reduction on stream teams (target 25% context switching decrease, 20% productivity gains).

Sustained cognitive load optimization requires continuous monitoring, threshold-based triggers for team boundary adjustments, and platform evolution prioritized by load reduction impact, enabling teams to maintain mastery and effectiveness.

narrativeContexts.context: Team Topologies provides simplified organizational vocabulary with four fundamental types (Stream-Aligned, Platform, Enabling, Complicated-Subsystem) as alternative to traditional hierarchies, designed to optimize value flow and software architecture through intentional communication structures.

Topology design applies fracture planes to define team boundaries with Domain-Driven Design bounded contexts as primary split, plus regulatory compliance, change cadence, team location, risk profile, performance isolation, technology (cautiously), and user personas as additional fracture planes. Team boundaries must align with cognitive capacity using domain heuristics (maximum 1 complex or 2-3 simple domains per team), avoiding monolithic anti-patterns. Organizational sensing enables continuous evolution through small incremental adjustments monthly based on triggers (software exceeding capacity, delivery cadence degradation, complex service dependencies) rather than massive annual reorganizations.

Mature topology design achieves predictable architectural outcomes through deliberate team structure, sustained fast flow with minimal dependencies, and self-steering adaptation to environment changes as competitive advantage.

narrativeContexts.context: Only three ways teams should interact, eliminating ambiguous coordination mandates and providing clear vocabulary for team relationships with different cognitive load costs and suitable contexts.

Collaboration mode suits discovery of new things (APIs, practices, technologies) with working closely together for defined period, high bandwidth but high cost, time-bounded with clear goals, limited to one collaboration per team at a time, leading to blurred boundaries and blended software responsibilities through Conway's Law. X-as-a-Service mode enables consuming well-defined component with minimal interaction, clear ownership boundaries, predictable delivery, low cognitive load on consumer, requiring well-chosen service boundaries and excellent DevEx (usability, reliability, versioning, documentation). Facilitating mode involves one team helping another learn/adopt practices/overcome impediments, empowerment focus making teams self-sufficient, no direct system building by facilitator, typical for enabling teams assisting stream-aligned teams.

Explicit interaction modes with strategic evolution enable fast flow by minimizing wasteful coordination while preserving necessary collaboration, with modes serving as organizational sensors signaling topology adjustment needs.

patternViews.name: Static Organization
patternViews.description: Starting state with fixed hierarchical teams and no topology awareness.

patternViews.name: Four Team Types Adopted
patternViews.description: Organization explicitly adopts Team Topologies vocabulary and begins cognitive load management.

patternViews.name: Explicit Interaction Modes
patternViews.description: Teams define clear interaction patterns and Team APIs, enabling effective collaboration.

patternViews.name: Sensing and Evolving
patternViews.description: Organization establishes feedback mechanisms for continuous topology adaptation.

patternViews.name: Self-Steering Organization
patternViews.description: Mature cybernetic system with predictable evolution and architecture co-evolution.
